output.title: Financial performance & operating leverage
output.summary: FY2026 revenue and operating income expanded while operating margin moved to 46.8%.

findings.headline: Scale translated into operating leverage
findings.detail: Revenue grew 17.8%; operating income grew 20.8%, a 3.0 percentage-point spread.

findings.headline: The three-year earnings base is materially larger
findings.detail: Revenue increased from $245.1B in FY2024 to $331.8B in FY2026; net income reached $133.7B.

findings.headline: Profitability remains exceptional but is not the whole cash story
findings.detail: Operating margin was 46.8% and net margin was 40.3%; the separate cash-flow analysis tests whether AI infrastructure spending converts those earnings into distributable cash.

caveats: Historical GAAP performance does not establish future growth or valuation.
diligence_questions: How much of FY2026 growth is durable consumption growth versus capacity catch-up or contract timing?
What revenue contribution and gross-margin profile does management expect from paid Copilot and agent workloads?

output.title: Quarterly, TTM & change intelligence
output.verdict: Growth remains strong; capital intensity governs cash conversion
output.summary: FY2026 Q4 revenue was $90.0B, 17.7% above the year-ago quarter; trailing revenue reached $331.8B.

findings.headline: Quarterly growth remains double digit
findings.detail: Revenue increased 17.7% year over year and 8.6% sequentially in FY2026 Q4; operating margin was 45.1%.

findings.headline: TTM scale is paired with exceptional infrastructure spend
findings.detail: Through FY2026 Q4, TTM CFO was $182.9B, capex was $115.9B, and conventional FCF was $67.0B.

findings.headline: Quarter construction reconciles to filed annual facts
findings.detail: All 24 available annual-to-quarter checks reconcile within tolerance; 36 quarter observations are explicitly derived from filed cumulative or annual facts.

caveats: TTM values are deterministic sums of four fiscal quarters and are not management guidance.
Q2/Q3 may be derived from cumulative interim facts; Q4 is annual less nine-month YTD only when both filed inputs exist.
Quarterly cash flow is seasonal and should not be annualized from a single period.
diligence_questions: Is year-over-year revenue acceleration converting to FCF after the full capacity-build cycle?
Which quarter-level changes reflect seasonality, investment marks, contract timing, or durable operations?
Do derived quarters reconcile to the face statements and footnotes after every new filing or amendment?

output.title: Filing timeline & disclosure-change triage
output.verdict: Machine triage narrows review; it does not replace a legal redline
output.summary: Compared the 10-K filed 2025-07-30 with the 10-K filed 2026-07-29 and surfaced 5 deterministic review signals.

findings.headline: Microsoft Cloud gross margin: reported metric changed
findings.detail: The deterministic comparison moved from 0.69 to 0.66 on a deterministic percentage extraction basis.

findings.headline: Datacenter capacity, energy, and GPUs: expanded signal
findings.detail: The deterministic comparison moved from 6 to 10 on a deterministic phrase-hit delta basis.

findings.headline: OpenAI and strategic-partner economics: expanded signal
findings.detail: The deterministic comparison moved from 14 to 30 on a deterministic phrase-hit delta basis.

caveats: Phrase-hit movement is a triage signal, not a legal redline or materiality conclusion.
Added or removed wording can reflect drafting, taxonomy, or document-structure changes.
A professional must inspect the linked filings before relying on any disclosure delta.
diligence_questions: Which added, removed, or expanded passages survive a paragraph-level professional redline?
Do recent 8-K items alter any thesis, risk, estimate, or disclosure-control conclusion?
Did definitions, segment presentation, accounting policies, or non-GAAP reconciliations change?

output.title: Segment & product economics
output.verdict: Cloud-led mix shift; consumer portfolio diverges
output.summary: Intelligent Cloud became a co-primary revenue engine in FY2026, while More Personal Computing contracted.

findings.headline: Intelligent Cloud is the incremental growth engine
findings.detail: Segment revenue reached $137.8B, growing 29.7% and representing 41.5% of group revenue.

findings.headline: Productivity remains a high-margin ballast
findings.detail: Productivity and Business Processes generated $83.9B of operating income at a 59.9% segment margin.

findings.headline: Portfolio dispersion requires separate underwriting
findings.detail: More Personal Computing revenue changed -1.1%; cloud and productivity momentum should not be used to mask weaker gaming, device, or consumer economics.

caveats: Microsoft recast prior segment information; comparisons use the presentation in the latest 10-K.
diligence_questions: What portion of Intelligent Cloud growth is AI workload demand, and what portion reflects non-AI Azure consumption?
Can More Personal Computing stabilize without structurally lower investment or further portfolio actions?
How should shared AI infrastructure cost be allocated across Azure, Microsoft 365 Copilot, GitHub, and consumer products?

output.title: Cash flow & AI capital intensity
output.verdict: Cash generation rose, but capex absorbed the increment
output.summary: Operating cash flow reached $182.9B, while capex rose to $115.9B and compressed conventional free cash flow.

findings.headline: Capex, not operating weakness, drove conventional FCF pressure
findings.detail: CFO grew 34.4%, but capex grew 79.6%; FCF moved from $71.6B to $67.0B.

findings.headline: The balance sheet now embeds a much larger infrastructure base
findings.detail: Net property and equipment increased 52.7%, making utilization, depreciation lives, energy availability, and hardware obsolescence central underwriting variables.

findings.headline: Reported CFO still covers accounting earnings
findings.detail: CFO was 1.37x net income, but stock compensation of $12.4B is a real ownership cost and is shown separately.

caveats: CFO less capex is a non-GAAP analytical measure and does not distinguish growth from maintenance capex.
Subtracting stock compensation from FCF is an ownership-economics lens, not a GAAP measure.
diligence_questions: What is the split between maintenance, contracted growth, and speculative AI capacity capex?
What utilization and token-price assumptions are required for new AI datacenters to earn the cost of capital?
How sensitive are useful lives and depreciation expense to accelerated GPU obsolescence?

output.title: Balance sheet, liquidity & credit capacity
output.verdict: Substantial liquidity; leases and build commitments matter
output.summary: Microsoft ended FY2026 with $76.8B of cash and short-term investments versus $40.3B of funded debt.

findings.headline: Funded-debt liquidity is strong
findings.detail: Cash and short-term investments exceeded funded debt by $36.5B; debt was 0.26x annual operating income.

findings.headline: Lease-adjusted obligations are economically relevant
findings.detail: Reported finance and operating lease liabilities total approximately $88.5B and should be included in capacity and fixed-charge analysis.

findings.headline: Backlog visibility is large but not cash in hand
findings.detail: Total remaining performance obligations were approximately $684.0B; timing, cancellation rights, cloud consumption, and margin realization determine its economic value.

caveats: RPO is not equivalent to contracted cash, recognized revenue, or profit.
diligence_questions: How much datacenter capacity is covered by non-cancellable customer commitments of comparable duration?
What are peak annual lease, purchase, power, and construction cash requirements under stress?

output.title: Capital allocation & ownership economics
output.summary: Capex and R&D totaled $151.5B, materially above $48.7B returned through dividends and repurchases.

findings.headline: Capital allocation is an AI reinvestment decision first
findings.detail: Capex plus R&D represented 45.7% of revenue, so future value depends on incremental returns from infrastructure and product investment.

findings.headline: Buybacks should be assessed net of employee equity issuance
findings.detail: Cash repurchases were $22.3B versus $12.4B of stock compensation; the net cash repurchase lens was $9.9B.

findings.headline: Distributions remain affordable but compete with capex
findings.detail: Dividends plus repurchases consumed 72.7% of conventional FCF in FY2026.

caveats: Stock compensation expense and repurchase cash outlays are not directly interchangeable period by period.
diligence_questions: What return threshold governs incremental AI datacenter commitments versus repurchases?
At what valuation does management view buybacks as accretive after stock-based compensation?

output.title: Valuation laboratory & reverse DCF
output.verdict: Premium valuation requires sustained FCF acceleration
output.summary: The indicative price of $496.82 sits above the illustrative base DCF of $344.16; this is a sensitivity framework, not a target price.

findings.headline: The market capitalizes a long duration of growth
findings.detail: Indicative P/E is 27.7x and EV/revenue is 11.0x; the earnings yield is 3.6% versus a 4.79% 10-year Treasury yield.

findings.headline: Reverse DCF makes the embedded requirement explicit
findings.detail: At the base discount and terminal assumptions, normalized FCF must compound approximately 23.3% annually for five years to support the indicative price.

findings.headline: Scenario dispersion is the decision, not a single point estimate
findings.detail: Illustrative values span $190.82 to $596.07 per share because AI capex, FCF growth, and discount rates dominate the result.

caveats: DCF outputs are illustrative and highly sensitive; they are not forecasts or investment recommendations.
Yahoo data is indicative; production decisions require a licensed price source.
Normalized FCF averages two years and does not separate maintenance from growth capex.
diligence_questions: What five-year FCF growth range is supportable under realistic AI pricing, utilization, and depreciation assumptions?
How should OpenAI/Anthropic investment gains and losses be excluded from normalized earnings?
What risk premium is appropriate for a hyperscaler during an unusually capital-intensive platform transition?
assumptions: Five explicit annual periods with constant FCF growth by scenario.
Terminal value uses the Gordon growth model; net cash is added to equity value.
Starting FCF is the average of the latest two fiscal years' CFO less capex.

output.title: Market, rate & macro risk
output.verdict: Momentum constructive; discount-rate sensitivity remains material
output.summary: MSFT returned -0.9% over the retrieved one-year window with 32.4% annualized realized volatility.

findings.headline: Equity duration is exposed to real and nominal yields
findings.detail: The 10-year nominal Treasury yield was 4.79% and the real yield was 2.44%; higher yields reduce the present value of long-dated AI cash flows.

findings.headline: Observed beta does not capture platform-transition risk
findings.detail: One-year daily beta was 0.97 with 0.38 correlation to the S&P 500; capacity, regulation, or AI-pricing shocks may not resemble the historical window.

findings.headline: Price trend is currently above key moving averages
findings.detail: The latest adjusted close was 13.5% from the 50-day average and 15.7% from the 200-day average.

caveats: Technical statistics use approximately one year of indicative adjusted prices and are not predictive.
diligence_questions: How should the equity risk premium change if AI capex remains elevated for longer than consensus expects?
What revenue and margin sensitivity should be applied under slower GDP growth or stronger U.S. dollar scenarios?

output.title: Peer operating benchmark
output.verdict: Top-tier margins; AI capex lowers current FCF conversion
output.summary: Microsoft ranks 1 of 6 on operating margin and 3 of 6 on conventional FCF margin in the selected cross-platform peer set.

findings.headline: Operating profitability compares favorably
findings.detail: Microsoft's 46.8% operating margin compares with a 32.0% peer median.

findings.headline: Current capex intensity changes the peer narrative
findings.detail: Microsoft invested 34.9% of revenue in capex versus a 22.7% median, depressing current FCF margin relative to accounting margins.

findings.headline: This is an operating benchmark, not a valuation comp set
findings.detail: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Apple, and Oracle have different fiscal calendars, segment mixes, capital structures, and accounting judgments.

caveats: Peers use each issuer's latest available annual 10-K period; fiscal calendars and business mixes differ.
diligence_questions: Which peers best match Azure infrastructure economics versus Microsoft 365 software economics?
Should capex be normalized by deployed capacity, revenue, or expected workload demand when comparing hyperscalers?

output.title: Accounting quality & earnings normalization
output.verdict: Strong cash conversion with material non-operating noise
output.summary: CFO was 1.37x net income, but non-operating income and investment marks widened the gap between operating and GAAP net-income growth.

findings.headline: Core cash conversion is strong
findings.detail: CFO exceeded net income by $49.2B and the accrual ratio was -7.1% of average assets.

findings.headline: Investment marks require normalized earnings
findings.detail: Other income/expense swung by $15.6B year over year; Microsoft separately disclosed a $5.0B FY2026 net-income impact from OpenAI investments.

findings.headline: Receivables grew faster than revenue
findings.detail: Accounts receivable grew 15.7% versus revenue growth of 17.8%; DSO was approximately 89 days at year-end.

caveats: Year-end DSO is affected by seasonality and fourth-quarter contract timing.
diligence_questions: What portion of receivables growth reflects Q4 seasonality, contract structure, or collection-cycle change?
Which investment gains and losses should be excluded from recurring earnings and valuation multiples?
How sensitive are reported margins to useful-life estimates for rapidly evolving AI infrastructure?

output.title: External audit & controls assurance
output.summary: The latest 10-K supports clean financial-statement and ICFR conclusions while identifying revenue recognition and tax as high-judgment areas.

findings.headline: External audit opinion is unmodified
findings.detail: Deloitte & Touche LLP reported that the financial statements present fairly in all material respects.

findings.headline: Internal control opinion is unmodified
findings.detail: The filing contains an unqualified auditor conclusion on internal control over financial reporting; reasonable assurance is not absolute assurance.

findings.headline: Critical audit matters identify the highest-judgment areas
findings.detail: Detected CAM topics: Revenue recognition, Uncertain tax positions. These require targeted contract, tax, model, and control testing rather than generic review.

caveats: An unmodified audit opinion is not a guarantee against fraud, future control failure, or forecast error.
This analysis does not reproduce or replace the auditor's report or perform audit procedures.
diligence_questions: How are standalone selling prices and performance obligations controlled for bundled cloud and AI contracts?
What audit procedures address consumption estimates, variable consideration, and free or optional AI services?
How are model governance and change controls evolving for AI-assisted financial processes?

output.title: Tax rate, controversy & policy exposure
output.verdict: Manageable current rate; concentrated controversy tail
output.summary: The FY2026 effective tax rate was 19.4%; uncertain tax positions and the IRS transfer-pricing dispute remain material diligence items.

findings.headline: Reported tax rate remains below the U.S. statutory rate
findings.detail: Tax expense was $32.2B on $165.9B of pretax income, an effective rate of 19.4%.

findings.headline: Transfer-pricing controversy is a material tail scenario
findings.detail: The filing discusses IRS proposed adjustments seeking approximately $28.9B plus penalties and interest; Microsoft disputes the adjustments.

findings.headline: Tax reserves require judgment
findings.detail: Gross unrecognized tax benefits were approximately $25.8B, so settlement timing and measurement can affect future effective rates and cash flows.

caveats: The proposed IRS amount is not an expected loss estimate; outcomes and timing are uncertain.
diligence_questions: What probability-weighted cash and rate scenarios should be assigned to the transfer-pricing dispute?
How will OECD Pillar Two, U.S. law changes, and geographic profit mix affect the normalized tax rate?
How much of deferred-tax asset growth depends on future taxable income and R&D capitalization rules?

output.title: Cloud, Copilot & AI infrastructure economics
output.verdict: Demand proof is strong; return-on-capital proof is still forming
output.summary: Azure exceeded $100B of fiscal revenue and Microsoft 365 Copilot passed 30M paid seats, while capex reached $115.9B.

findings.headline: Commercial demand indicators are unusually strong
findings.detail: Q4 Azure growth was 43.0%; commercial RPO reached $678B and grew 84.0%.

findings.headline: Paid Copilot adoption is now measurable
findings.detail: Microsoft disclosed more than 30M Microsoft 365 Copilot paid seats, improving evidence beyond product-launch narratives.

findings.headline: Unit economics remain obscured by shared infrastructure
findings.detail: Capex equaled 34.9% of revenue and PP&E grew 52.7%; segment disclosure does not isolate AI inference revenue, gross margin, utilization, or return on deployed capital.

caveats: Azure revenue and Copilot seats are management-reported operating metrics and do not disclose standalone profitability.
RPO includes timing and mix effects and should not be treated as immediate AI revenue.
diligence_questions: What are AI infrastructure utilization, power, depreciation, and gross-margin curves by workload cohort?
What portion of Copilot seats are incremental versus bundled, discounted, trial, or substitution revenue?
What customer concentration, model-provider, and GPU-supplier dependencies sit behind RPO growth?
How quickly can software and custom-silicon efficiency offset token-price compression?

output.title: Regulatory, cyber & operational risk register
output.verdict: No single red flag; several enterprise-scale tail risks
output.summary: The filing supports a concentrated risk register around AI capital returns, cyber resilience, regulation, strategic partners, tax, and infrastructure supply.

findings.headline: AI return risk is broader than demand risk
findings.detail: The key failure mode is not merely weak demand; it is strong demand monetized below the fully loaded cost of capacity, energy, depreciation, and model economics.

findings.headline: Cyber risk is systemic to the franchise
findings.detail: Identity, cloud, security, and productivity products make operational resilience and secure-by-design execution both a customer promise and a financial dependency.

findings.headline: Regulatory risks interact rather than stand alone
findings.detail: Antitrust, privacy, AI safety, content, sovereignty, export-control, and government-contract requirements can alter product design, cost, and distribution simultaneously.

caveats: Likelihood and impact labels are analyst judgments, not management guidance or probabilities.
diligence_questions: What board-level risk appetite and leading indicators govern AI capacity commitments?
How are Secure Future Initiative outcomes independently tested and linked to executive accountability?
What are quantified revenue and cost sensitivities for major AI, privacy, competition, and sovereignty rules?
What contingency exists for model-provider, GPU, power, or region-specific service disruption?

risk_register.rationale: Demand can remain strong while pricing, utilization, depreciation, or capacity timing depress returns.
Microsoft operates mission-critical identity, cloud, productivity, and security infrastructure at global scale.
Rules can constrain bundling, data use, model deployment, sovereign-cloud design, or acquisition strategy.
Reciprocal economics, capacity rights, model access, and investment accounting affect both operations and reported earnings.
The IRS transfer-pricing dispute creates a large but uncertain cash and earnings tail.
Capacity depends on scarce chips, power, networking, land, permits, construction, and supplier execution.
More Personal Computing is not sharing equally in cloud-led growth and faces distinct platform competition.
Global revenue and infrastructure expose results to currency, trade controls, sovereignty, and geopolitical change.

synthesis.recommendation: CONTINUE DILIGENCE — DO NOT RELY ON A SINGLE VALUATION CASE
synthesis.summary: Microsoft's FY2026 Q4 revenue grew 17.7% year over year, extending FY growth of 17.8%. TTM revenue was $331.8B, while $115.9B of TTM capex reduced conventional TTM FCF to $67.0B. All 24 annual-to-quarter checks reconciled, and annual filing triage surfaced 5 review signals. The indicative price requires approximately 23.3% five-year FCF compounding under the disclosed reverse-DCF assumptions.
synthesis.confidence_label: uncalibrated analytical confidence — not a probability

bull: Latest-quarter revenue growth of 17.7% and TTM revenue of $331.8B show that demand remains visible in filed results, not only management KPIs.
Azure growth of 43.0% and commercial RPO growth of 84.0% provide unusually strong forward demand evidence.
Paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats exceeded 30M, creating a measurable application-layer monetization path.
Operating leverage and high-margin productivity software can finance the infrastructure transition without balance-sheet stress.
base: Cloud and AI sustain above-market growth, but TTM capex intensity of 34.9% keeps FCF conversion below historical software norms.
Valuation outcomes depend more on realized FCF and discount rates than on headline AI adoption metrics alone.
The 5 detected annual disclosure signals are triage inputs; the appropriate workflow is professional redline review and explicit trigger monitoring.
bear: Capacity is built ahead of durable demand, token prices fall faster than unit costs, or useful lives shorten, reducing return on invested capital.
Cyber, antitrust, privacy, sovereignty, tax, or model-partner events impose simultaneous revenue, cost, and reputation pressure.
TTM FCF of $67.0B fails to reaccelerate while capacity commitments and higher-for-longer rates pressure long-duration value.
